Why do they sleep like this? Dolphins are mammals, just like humans. This means they need to breathe air at the surface. If they fully fell asleep underwater, they could drown. So one half of their brain controls breathing while the other half rests.
Dolphins also keep one eye open while sleeping. This way, they can watch out for dangers like sharks. After a few hours, the two sides of the brain switch jobs. The top spot might shock you!\nAccording to one famous study by ESPN, boxing was ranked as the most demanding sport overall. Boxers need incredible strength, endurance, speed, and quick thinking all at the same time. They also face actual physical danger every match. Few other sports require so many different abilities working together perfectly under pressure.\nIce hockey came in second on the list. However, throughout history, several strange events have come and gone. Some seem almost too silly to believe. These forgotten Olympic sports show how much our idea of athletic competition has changed over time. ① For instance, art competitions were part of the Olympics from 1912 to 1948! Athletes won medals for painting, music, and even architecture. ② The rule was that artworks had to be related to sports themes. ③ Another strange one was 'club swinging'. This condition is different from a food allergy, although many people confuse the two. Food intolerances rarely threaten your life, but they can cause significant discomfort over time.
Lactose intolerance is one of the most common examples. Approximately 65% of adults worldwide have difficulty digesting dairy products. Their bodies lack a particular enzyme needed to break down milk sugar. Symptoms typically include stomach pain, bloating, and digestive issues within hours of consumption.
Scientists are still investigating why intolerances develop. Genetics certainly play a role, but environmental factors matter too. Modern processed foods contain many additives that our ancestors never encountered. Some researchers believe gradual exposure to small amounts can sometimes help. Others recommend avoiding problem foods entirely. The brief delay between seeing food and eating builds anticipation, releasing chemicals that enhance pleasure. It's similar to how looking at a wrapped gift increases excitement before opening it. The brain registers the meal as more special.
However, this habit also has darker psychological aspects. Many people photograph meals primarily to share online, hoping to impress others. The colorful shapes and seemingly random lines often appear simple enough that children could create them. Yet abstract masterpieces sell for millions of dollars each. Why do art experts value these unusual artworks so highly? Understanding abstract art requires looking beyond the surface appearance.\nAbstract art emerged in the early 20th century as artists explored entirely new forms of expression. Traditional painting had focused on representing realistic scenes accurately for centuries. Photography then took over this descriptive function during the 1800s. Artists needed new ways to communicate emotions and ideas that cameras couldn't capture. Abstract painting allowed direct expression of feelings without depicting physical objects.\nFamous abstract painters like Wassily Kandinsky believed colors could represent music visually. Jackson Pollock developed unique techniques of dripping paint to express emotional energy. Each abstract artwork involves carefully considered decisions about color, shape, and balance. Creating effective abstract paintings actually requires significant skill and training. The apparent simplicity hides decades of development and conscious choices. {"articles":[{"title":"왜 어떤 나라는 시간을 안 지킬까?","content":"In Korea, arriving late to an appointment is considered seriously rude. Most Koreans plan their schedules carefully and feel uncomfortable when others are even slightly delayed. However, this strict attitude toward time isn't universal across cultures. In many countries, being significantly late is completely normal and expected behavior.
In parts of South America and Africa, people typically arrive 30 minutes to an hour after the scheduled time. This isn't considered rude at all—rather, it's expected. The cultures place greater value on personal relationships than strict schedules. If someone is engaged in meaningful conversation, leaving abruptly would be considered impolite. Time, in these cultures, is fundamentally a flexible concept.
Researchers have proposed several explanations for these differences. Cultures with industrial histories tend to value precise timing more strongly. Agricultural societies traditionally followed natural rhythms rather than clocks. Geographic factors and economic systems also play roles. Whatever the causes, understanding these cultural differences helps prevent misunderstandings. When traveling internationally, learning local time customs is just as important as learning the language.","vocabulary":[],"sentenceList":[],"keySentences":[],"questions":[],"aiGenerated":false},{"title":"이름이 직업이 되는 이유","content":"Have you ever noticed how some people's names match their professions perfectly? A baker named Mr. Baker, or a doctor named Dr. Healer might seem like funny coincidences. However, researchers have discovered that this happens far more often than random chance would predict. There's actually a name for this strange phenomenon—nominative determinism.
A scientific study examined the names of professionals across various fields. The findings were genuinely surprising. Dentists were significantly more likely to be named 'Denis' than statistical probability suggests. Similar patterns appeared in many professions worldwide. People named Lawrence often became lawyers. Those called Robert frequently chose careers involving rocks or robotics.
Psychologists offer two main explanations for this peculiar pattern. First, people unconsciously gravitate toward professions that sound familiar to them. A child named Smith might feel naturally drawn to metalwork or craftsmanship. Second, others may treat individuals according to expectations created by their names. Whether the cause is internal or external, our names appear to influence our lives more than most people realize.","vocabulary":[],"sentenceList":[],"keySentences":[],"questions":[],"aiGenerated":false},{"title":"전 세계의 신기한 결혼식 풍습","content":"Weddings are deeply meaningful ceremonies in every culture, though traditions vary dramatically across the globe. Some customs that seem perfectly normal in one country might appear absolutely strange elsewhere. These differences reveal much about how various societies view marriage, family, and community connections.
In certain regions of India, brides paint elaborate patterns on their hands using a natural dye called henna. The designs can take six hours to complete and remain visible for weeks. Meanwhile, in Scotland, couples participate in a tradition called 'blackening'. Friends throw various unpleasant substances at the bride and groom before the wedding. This is supposed to prepare them for marriage's difficulties.
In certain African cultures, families exchange livestock as part of the marriage agreement. The number of animals given reflects respect for the bride's family. South Korea has its own traditions—wedding guests give money in white envelopes, while in some Asian cultures, the wedding banquet must continue for several days. Despite the variations, all wedding ceremonies share one essential meaning: celebrating two people who choose to share their lives together.","vocabulary":[],"sentenceList":[],"keySentences":[],"questions":[],"aiGenerated":false}]}

{"articles":[{"title":"색맹이었던 위대한 예술가","content":"Have you ever wondered how a color-blind painter creates beautiful artwork? Many famous artists throughout history actually struggled with various forms of color vision problems. Yet they produced some of the world's most celebrated paintings. Their unusual perspectives often led to revolutionary artistic styles that influenced generations.
The famous Spanish painter Joan Miro is believed to have had color blindness. Some art historians argue this condition influenced his distinctive bright color choices. He used vivid contrasts that other artists might have avoided. Vincent van Gogh, though probably not color-blind, may have seen colors differently due to medication. This could partially explain his unique yellow-dominated paintings during certain periods.
Modern technology now helps color-blind artists work more effectively. Special glasses can enable them to distinguish colors they couldn't see before. Computer software can also identify and label colors precisely. However, some artists actually prefer working without these aids. They believe their unusual perception gives their work a distinctive character. Sometimes, what seems like a limitation becomes a source of genuine artistic strength.","vocabulary":[],"sentenceList":[],"keySentences":[],"questions":[],"aiGenerated":false},{"title":"디지털 예술가가 되는 법","content":"Becoming a successful artist used to require expensive supplies and years of formal training. Today, the digital revolution has completely changed how art is created and shared. Anyone with a tablet and creative imagination can now produce professional-quality artwork. This transformation has democratized art in ways previous generations couldn't have imagined.
Digital art tools offer numerous advantages over traditional methods. Artists can experiment with countless techniques without wasting paper or paint. Mistakes can be corrected instantly by pressing 'undo'. Multiple versions of the same artwork can be saved easily. Online platforms also allow digital artists to reach worldwide audiences directly. They can build careers without needing approval from traditional art galleries.
However, digital art faces some unique challenges as well. Many critics argue that physical paintings hold a value that digital files cannot match. The question of copying remains particularly complicated. Anyone can technically save a digital image with one click. Recently, blockchain technology has emerged as a possible solution. These developments suggest that the definition of art itself continues to evolve dramatically.","vocabulary":[],"sentenceList":[],"keySentences":[],"questions":[],"aiGenerated":false},{"title":"미술관이 그림을 도난당하는 이유","content":"Art theft is significantly more common than most people realize. Every year, valuable paintings worth millions of dollars disappear from museums and private collections worldwide. The most famous example remains the 1990 Boston museum theft. Despite enormous rewards and worldwide investigations, none of the stolen masterpieces have ever been recovered after more than three decades.
Why do thieves continue stealing artwork that's almost impossible to sell openly? Researchers have identified several motivations behind these crimes. Some criminals genuinely believe they can find buyers in secret markets. Others steal art to use as collateral in illegal business deals. Surprisingly, some stolen pieces end up trading hands among criminals for decades. They function almost like a form of underground currency.
Museums have responded by significantly improving their security systems. Modern facilities use motion sensors, hidden cameras, and even invisible identification marks. Some valuable paintings travel between exhibitions with armed guards. Despite these precautions, determined criminals occasionally succeed. The constant battle between security experts and art thieves continues evolving with new technology each year, creating an endless cat-and-mouse game.","vocabulary":[],"sentenceList":[],"keySentences":[],"questions":[],"aiGenerated":false}]}

{"articles":[{"title":"AI가 의사를 대체할 수 있을까?","content":"Artificial intelligence is rapidly entering medical fields worldwide. AI systems can now diagnose certain diseases more accurately than experienced doctors. Some hospitals have integrated AI into their daily operations. However, this development raises serious questions about the future of medicine. Will artificial intelligence eventually replace human doctors entirely?
Recent studies have produced fascinating results. AI consistently outperforms human specialists at recognizing patterns in medical images. Specifically, AI can identify certain cancers in their early stages with remarkable precision. Computer systems can analyze thousands of images in minutes. They never get tired or distracted, unlike human doctors working long shifts.
Despite these advantages, medical experts argue that AI cannot truly replace human doctors. Patients need emotional support that machines cannot provide. Complex cases often require intuition developed through years of experience. Furthermore, AI systems sometimes make unusual mistakes that humans would never make. The future probably involves doctors and AI working together as partners. Each can do what they do best, ultimately providing better care for patients.","vocabulary":[],"sentenceList":[],"keySentences":[],"questions":[],"aiGenerated":false},{"title":"인터넷의 어두운 면","content":"The internet has transformed our world in extraordinary ways over recent decades. We can now communicate instantly with people anywhere on Earth. We have access to virtually all human knowledge through our phones. Yet this incredible technology has a darker side that affects millions of users. Mental health experts are increasingly worried about the internet's psychological impact.
Numerous studies have linked excessive internet use to depression and anxiety in young people. Social media particularly contributes to these problems. Users constantly compare themselves to others' carefully curated online lives. They see only the highlights of others' experiences, never the ordinary or difficult moments. This creates unrealistic expectations and feelings of inadequacy.
Researchers also worry about the addictive nature of modern platforms. Tech companies hire psychologists specifically to make their apps more engaging. Notifications and rewards trigger the same brain chemicals as gambling. Some users now describe difficulty controlling their phone usage. Several countries have begun teaching digital wellness in schools. Learning to use technology wisely has become an essential life skill for younger generations.","vocabulary":[],"sentenceList":[],"keySentences":[],"questions":[],"aiGenerated":false},{"title":"양자컴퓨터의 시대","content":"Traditional computers store information using simple ones and zeros. They've grown incredibly powerful over the past decades, but they're approaching their physical limits. Scientists believe quantum computers represent the next major technological revolution. These machines work on completely different principles, potentially solving problems that would take regular computers thousands of years.
Quantum computers use particles called 'qubits' instead of standard bits. Unlike regular bits, qubits can exist in multiple states simultaneously. This unusual property allows quantum computers to process enormous amounts of information at once. They could revolutionize fields including medicine, security, and weather prediction. Major technology companies are investing billions in this developing area.
However, building practical quantum computers presents enormous challenges. The qubits require extremely cold temperatures to function properly. Even tiny disturbances can disrupt their calculations. Currently, quantum computers exist mainly in research laboratories worldwide. Within twenty years, they might become commonly available. The transition could be as significant as the original development of personal computers in the 1970s. Our digital future remains both exciting and unpredictable.","vocabulary":[],"sentenceList":[],"keySentences":[],"questions":[],"aiGenerated":false}]}

These forgotten competitions reveal how dramatically our understanding of athletic competition has transformed.\nIn the early 20th century, the Olympics included tug-of-war as a serious competitive event. Teams from various countries competed by pulling ropes across a line. Live pigeon shooting was also briefly featured, with athletes shooting real birds. Even running deer shooting, where targets moved like animals, appeared in several Olympics. These violent events were eventually removed due to public objections.\nOther vanished events seem peculiar but harmless. 'Plunge for distance' involved swimmers diving and floating motionlessly for distance. Hot air balloon competitions tested who could fly farthest in time. Music, painting, and architecture competitions awarded actual Olympic medals from 1912 to 1948. These artistic events were eventually removed because competitors were professional artists rather than amateurs. People meet friends, conduct business, and study at coffee shops constantly. However, the original purpose of these establishments was quite different. Coffee shops emerged as revolutionary social spaces that fundamentally transformed how people interacted in society.
The first coffee shops appeared in the Middle East during the 15th century. Initially, religious leaders strongly opposed these gathering places. They feared coffee shops would distract believers from religious devotion. When coffee arrived in Europe during the 1600s, it created similar controversy. London's first coffee shops were called 'penny universities' because customers could learn from intellectual conversations for the price of a single coffee.
These establishments became centers of political and scientific debate quickly. Many famous discoveries and revolutions began with discussions in coffee shops. Newton supposedly developed several theories during coffee shop conversations. The French Revolution was partially planned in Parisian cafes. Reading and detailed work were nearly impossible for older adults. The simple invention of glasses dramatically transformed civilization in ways most people never consider.
Early glasses were extremely primitive and uncomfortable by modern standards. Two separate lenses connected by a wooden frame had to be held in front of the eyes. People constantly grew tired holding them while reading lengthy documents. Practical glasses that stayed on the face weren't developed until centuries later. By the 18th century, designs included supports that hooked over the ears. This innovation made glasses practical for everyday use throughout entire days.
Glasses fundamentally extended productive working lifespans for educated people. Without them, scholars could only work efficiently when young. Travelers often carried letters between cities as personal favors, sometimes delivering them weeks or months late. The eventual creation of postal systems revolutionized human communication permanently.
The ancient Persian Empire developed one of the earliest sophisticated postal systems around 500 BCE. Royal messengers carried important documents across vast distances quickly. They used relay stations where fresh horses awaited tired messengers. This system inspired similar networks in many ancient civilizations. The Roman Empire built upon Persian innovations to create an even more extensive communication network across Europe.

Few people know about solar storms. Solar storms start with an explosion on the sun. These explosions are more powerful than the biggest nuclear bomb. When they occur, Earth is sometimes affected. However, thanks to a unique layer around Earth, solar storms cannot hit Earth directly.
This is why we don’t see or feel them like a regular storm. They only disturb satellites and communication systems. Some solar storms even have a positive effect. They cause a beautiful phenomenon known as an aurora in some areas.

It happens because the brain needs extra time to work when it handles conflicting information. In this experiment, the word *red* is written in yellow. The word’s meaning and its color are conflicting. When there is conflicting information, the brain generally does the more familiar job first. The brain is more familiar with reading words than with naming colors. So words are recognized more quickly than colors. However, the experiment asks you to say the color, not the word. {"articles":[{"title":"오믈렛에 이런 유래가?","content":"An omelette, or omelet, is a simple egg dish. It is made by quickly frying beaten eggs in butter or oil. There is an interesting story about the origin of the word *omelette*.
Long ago, the king of Spain was taking a walk. He felt hungry, so he went into a farmer’s house and asked the man to serve him a meal quickly. The farmer only had a couple of eggs. So he hurriedly fried the eggs in oil in a pan for the king. “Quel homme leste!” the hungry king shouted. When you eat something, the scent of the food goes into your nose and stimulates the nerve cells in it. Then these send information about the taste to the brain. However, when your nose is stuffed, the scent cannot reach the nerve cells because of the mucus. If a predator attacks it, an explosion occurs inside its body! There is a popping sound, and a hot liquid shoots out. This liquid scares away larger predators. It can even kill smaller ones. If a toad swallows a bombardier beetle, the beetle sprays this liquid inside the toad. The toad vomits, and the beetle escapes safely.
The honeybee is another amazing insect. It builds honeycombs from wax and stores honey in them. All honeycombs are made with the same shape—the hexagon. Hexagons fit together perfectly, without any space between them. If the honeybee used circles instead, there would be a lot of wasted space between them. Triangles and squares can fit together like hexagons. But they require more wax and have less space for the honey. First, rain creates a shallow pond. At night, the water at the surface of the pond freezes, and the ice surrounds the rocks. During the day, however, the ice starts to melt, breaking up into large sheets that push against the rocks. Of course, this alone isn’t enough to move the rocks. “As you know, my web catches prey. But look closer. Each stitch catches bad dreams, too! Remember my technique, Nokomis, and use it to weave your own webs.
